newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble dips, T-bill sales attract fewer funds.
newsitem.headline: Rouble dips, T-bill sales attract fewer funds.

text.p: The rouble eased in lively trading on Tuesday on speculative demand from banks and dealers said Wednesday's Treasury bill auctions had failed to soak up roubles from the market, as usually happened.
The central bank is holding two T-bill auctions on Wednesday for a total of 10.5 trillion roubles of six-month paper.
"Some banks opened short dollar positions yesterday as they expected it to fall (ahead of the auctions)," one dealer said.
"It eased shortly in the morning but the rouble supply seems plentiful so the dollar has come up to the upper level of the central bank rates," he added.
A European Trade Bank dealer said: "The dollar's upward trend continues as banks must have considered the auctions fairly unattractive and they are investing in dollars."

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,346-48 per dollar compared with an early 5,335-38 and 5,341-44 late on Monday. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,350-52 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,338-40.
The central bank said it had set 5,312/5,352 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Monday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 20-30 percent compared with 5-10 percent late yesterday.
Dealers said the rouble was likely to ease further on Wednesday as Wednesday's government bond auctions were seen unable to decrease the supply on the rouble-dollar market.
